title: A lithium-ion cell discharging
caption: On discharge, lithium leaves the graphite negative electrode as Li⁺ and electrons; the Li⁺ crosses the electrolyte and the electrons go round the external circuit to the cobalt oxide positive electrode, where both are taken in. Charging reverses this.
alt: A cell with a graphite electrode on the left and a lithium cobalt oxide electrode on the right; Li⁺ ions move left to right through the electrolyte and electrons through the device.
description: Negative electrode (anode on discharge): LiC₆ → Li⁺ + C₆ + e⁻.
Positive electrode (cathode): CoO₂ + Li⁺ + e⁻ → LiCoO₂.

vessel.label: organic electrolyte with a lithium salt
